method_and_proof_review: Money aggregates explicitly specify instruments and holders; reserves are bank assets/central-bank liabilities, while customer deposits are bank liabilities and nonbank assets. Existing-asset transactions, financial claims and production are kept distinct.

The real opportunity cost is independently recovered by subtracting two final purchasing-power factors: q=(i_bill-i_deposit)/(1+inflation). The objective values future wealth linearly and expresses convenience in matching future-good units. Strict quadratic curvature and projection onto [0,w] establish the complete interior, zero, wealth-cap and zero-wealth cases. The inferred corner spread is a set, not point identification.

Every loan, interbank funding, payment, central advance and repayment has an explicit counterpart. Pledged collateral remains the commercial bank asset. Consolidation cancels precisely the internal interbank, reserve and advance positions; outside government and nonbank claims and book equity remain. Loan write-down is not represented as automatic legal forgiveness.

Capital, accounting equity, economic solvency and payment liquidity have distinct meanings. The fixed risk-weight-one capital inequality and full-outflow reserve/funding bound define a feasible interval rather than an optimal lending choice. Existing negative capital headroom is a violation, not adequate capitalization with zero new lending.

The reserve-demand model distinguishes base supply from total reserves after facility use, enforces comparable eligible outside options, and explicitly selects minimum necessary lending. The piecewise solution is continuous/nonincreasing across active ceiling, slope, floor, inactive ceiling and collapsed corridor. The chapter states why equal administered rates alone do not select facility quantity. Limited collateral access changes assumptions and can break the ceiling; ineligibility/frictions can weaken the floor.

The lending quote solves a strictly increasing expected-receipt inequality for p<1. The equivalent net-cost identity is (1-p)*i_loan=i_funding+c+p*(1-recovery); the p=1 case is handled separately. A quote is neither proof of willing demand nor of feasible loan quantity, and default probabilities are explicitly held fixed rather than silently assumed invariant under a general lending policy.

Exact realized and expected real gross returns are separated from a ratio of mean gross factors and the small-rate subtraction. The risky Euler qualification retains marginal utility covariance. Bond price sensitivity fixes the payoff and required yield rather than treating every yield as the policy rate.

All open interpretation tasks specify causal mechanisms, counterfactuals, timing and concrete threats. No current rate/regulation, jurisdiction-wide hard reserve floor, complete regulatory framework or measured transmission coefficient is fabricated.
